analysis: The PR is documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md bumps the 'Last updated' date and rewrites the forced tool_choice paragraph (head lines ~2017-2040). The supplied units (base lines 806-1611) are unchanged surrounding text; the changed hunk is at base ~2017, outside the supplied excerpts but visible in the patch. No code, config, key handling, attestation, cache storage or authorization behavior changes, so the PR cannot regress T-041 or the provider/coordinator boundary controls (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011). The new prose describes forced tool_choice routing via `tool_constraint_models` (coordinator routes only to listed builds), a per-build `model_type` catalog, `.structuredPostValidation` strategy, and that `NativeToolStreamRouter` drops framing whitespace (space/tab/CR/LF) around call frames while any other visible text is a 422 `tool_choice` violation. These claims are consistent with a fail-closed validation posture and do not weaken documented mitigations. Unverified contracts, since the implementing code (`ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift`, `NativeToolStreamRouter`, coordinator routing on `tool_constraint_models`) was not supplied: that the docs match the actual implementation, and that the whitespace-stripping does not allow hidden content to be smuggled past `ToolConstraintValidation.validate`. These are documentation-accuracy questions, not security regressions. The threat model needs no update for this PR. No findings.
